_comment: Source of truth for the Google Workspace Marketplace SDK listing and the OAuth consent screen. Nothing here is applied automatically -- Google exposes no write API for either -- but a human pastes from this file (see marketplace/RUNBOOK.md), and tools/check-listing.sh keeps it consistent with src/appsscript.json, deployment.json, and the assets it references.

app.name: Polyglot Slides
app.shortDescription: Translate any selection, slide, or whole deck into several languages with one click.
app._emailComment: Two addresses because Google asks for two with different rules. supportEmail is the public one (consent-screen 'User support email', Marketplace SDK developer email): a dropdown limited to the publishing account itself or a Google Group it manages, so it is the help@sprue.works group. contactEmail is the consent-screen 'Developer contact information': free text, where Google emails about verification and project changes. Also a Google Group, so no personal address is published and readers can be added later; it must accept external posts or Google's mail bounces silently.
app._postInstallTipComment: Store Listing 'Post-install tip' (required). Shown to users right after install, so it names the exact menu path from src/Code.js. Google documents no length limit for this field (the sibling shortDescription is documented at 200); check-listing.sh caps it at 200 as the conservative analog.
app.postInstallTip: Open a deck, then Extensions → Polyglot Slides → Open sidebar to pick your languages.

deployment._comment: LEGACY POINTER (#29). The Marketplace SDK Editor-add-on form has no deployment-ID field: it pins the Project Script ID (.clasp.json#scriptId) plus a script VERSION NUMBER, which a human bumps after each release (RUNBOOK section 4). tools/check-listing.sh still asserts this pointer resolves, so it stays until #29 replaces it with the script ID + published version.

oauth._comment: Must equal src/appsscript.json oauthScopes exactly; check-listing.sh fails otherwise. Google classifies script.container.ui as SENSITIVE (seen in the consent-screen Data access table, 2026-09-02), so OAuth verification is brand verification plus sensitive-scope review (justification + demo video). Neither scope is restricted, so no CASA security assessment.

assets._comment: Sizes are what the Marketplace SDK App Configuration / Store Listing and the OAuth consent screen ask for. Icons are rendered from icon.svg by tools/render-icons.sh. Screenshots are captured by hand (RUNBOOK step 7) at 1280x800 and listed in screenshots.json.
assets._cardBannerComment: Store Listing 'Application card banner', required at exactly 220x140. Rendered from banner.svg by tools/render-icons.sh; landscape sibling of icon.svg, not a rescale of it.

distribution._comment: Pick one before publishing. 'private' = visible only inside the publishing Workspace domain (no Google review; admins can install for everyone). 'unlisted' = Marketplace review + OAuth brand verification, installable by any Google account via the listing link.
